review_status: reviewed 2026-11-14 - profile checked against FWC species biology; Atlantic state/federal limits checked against current FWC snapper guidance

profile.size: Commonly reaches about 24 inches and 10 lb; larger fish occur offshore.
profile.swimming_depth: Occurs from shallow coastal and estuarine habitat to offshore reef and shelf waters; documented depth range extends to about 180 m.
profile.behavior: Uses a broad range of coastal structure, including mangroves, seagrass, reefs and artificial structure. Juveniles commonly occupy estuarine nursery habitat and may enter freshwater; adults also occur offshore around reefs. Spawning occurs offshore during summer.
profile.spawning: June through August according to FWC's Florida species profile.
profile.habitat: Coastal, estuarine and shelf waters; mangrove shorelines, seagrass beds, reefs and artificial structure.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, ideal for mangrove snapper.
factors.value_notes: The regional essential-fish-habitat assessment reports adult gray snapper occurrence at 13.4–32.5 °C across estuarine, nearshore, and offshore environments. This is a broad occurrence envelope, not a preferred temperature interval or South Florida SST response curve; it does not validate 20–31 °C / 24–29 °C as an optimum.

factors.reason_template: Structure is {value}, perfect cover for mangrove snapper.
factors.value_notes: Florida Museum and the regional EFH assessment describe gray snapper using mangroves, coral/rocky ledges, reefs, and hard/soft bottom habitats. This supports broad coastal structure association, but the sources do not validate every preferred category (especially wrecks/artificial reefs) or their numeric score ordering.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, inside mangrove snapper depth zone.
factors.value_notes: The EFH assessment reports adult occurrence from 0–180 m, while the profile's 0.5–50 m range and 2–30 m ideal represent a shallow coastal subset. This may be appropriate for an inshore/estuarine model but does not represent the full species depth distribution or validate the exact ideal band.

text.night: It is night, when nocturnal feeding is high.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

text.rising: The tide is rising, bringing in fresh water and bait.
text.falling: The tide is falling, flushing bait out through structure.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.

regulations.summary: Atlantic Florida: 10 in total length in state waters and 12 in in federal waters; 5 per person in state waters or 10 per person in federal waters, within the 10-snapper aggregate; open year-round.
regulations.min_size: 10 inches total length (Atlantic state waters); 12 inches total length (federal waters)
regulations.bag_limit: 5 per person per day in Atlantic state waters; 10 per person per day in federal waters; counts toward the 10-snapper aggregate
regulations.jurisdiction: Florida Atlantic state waters and adjacent federal waters; special rules apply in Biscayne National Park
regulations.source_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
regulations.notes: Atlantic state-water size and bag limits differ from federal-water limits. Biscayne National Park has additional species-specific rules; verify park limits before harvest.
